description: This file contains Python code designed to analyze git commit history and diffs to identify downstream commits that are not upstreamed. It defines functions and a class to execute git commands, parse their outputs, and identify commits unique to the downstream branch, particularly focusing on changes visible in diffs between branches.

classes.name: CommitFinder
classes.description: A class that encapsulates methods to find commit hashes for a specific file that are present in the diff between upstream and downstream branches.

methods.name: git(args)
methods.description: Executes a git command with specified arguments and returns its output.

methods.name: __init__(self, working_dir, upstream, downstream)
methods.description: Initializes a CommitFinder instance with working directory and branch names.

methods.name: __call__(self, filename)
methods.description: Returns a set of commit hashes that have made changes to a specific file in the specified diff between upstream and downstream branches.

methods.name: find_insertion_commits(upstream, downstream, working_dir)
methods.description: Finds commits that insert lines on top of the upstream baseline across all changed files.

methods.name: find(upstream, downstream, working_dir)
methods.description: Main function that identifies downstream commits missing upstream, based on rev-list output.

methods.name: main()
methods.description: Entry point that parses command-line arguments and outputs downstream commits not present upstream.
